$comment: Checks every generated site gets, whatever the scenario. Same shape as a spec's `rubric`: recall items must be present, precision audits count supported vs unsupported items, pass checks are PASS/FAIL.

imagery: At least one image, illustration, icon set, or inline SVG that visibly relates to the subject of the site

precision.items: images, illustrations, icons, and decorative graphics
precision.supported: relates to the subject of the site and actually renders (the file exists in `./site/`, or the SVG/CSS is inline)
precision.unsupported: generic filler unrelated to the subject, or a broken or missing image reference

functional: `site/index.html` exists and opens directly in a browser without a build step
Every local stylesheet, script, and image the site references resolves to a file in `./site/`
Every nav link and in-page anchor points at a page or section that exists
Every button and form does something: buttons are wired up, and forms have an action or a clearly marked placeholder
js-errors: Scripts are syntactically valid and don't reference undefined elements, functions, or variables. If a headless browser is available, load each page and check the console; otherwise read the scripts. PASS if the site has no JavaScript
Interactive behaviour (menu toggles, tabs, carousels, form handling) runs without throwing. PASS if the site has none
mobile: At a 375px-wide viewport nothing forces horizontal scrolling: no fixed widths wider than the screen, and images scale down
The layout adapts at narrow widths (media queries, flex/grid wrapping, or fluid units) instead of shrinking the desktop layout
Navigation stays usable on mobile (collapses, wraps, or stays compact) and tap targets are roughly 44px or well spaced
accessibility: Each page has exactly one `<h1>`, and headings don't skip levels
Every meaningful image has descriptive `alt` text; decorative images have `alt=""` or are CSS backgrounds
Body text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) against its background. Compute it from the CSS color values
Button and link text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text)
Interactive elements are real `<a>` or `<button>` elements (no clickable `<div>`s) and every form field has a label
visual: Body text is at least 16px, with line height around 1.4–1.8 and lines under ~80 characters
Uses at most three font families, with a clear size step between headings and body text
Spacing between sections and elements follows a consistent scale rather than one-off values, and content isn't pressed against the viewport edges
The headline and primary call to action are the most visually prominent elements in the first screen
The color palette is cohesive (a small set of colors used consistently) and suits the subject
